We encourage you to come and meet us, look around and see if St John’s is the school for your child or a community partner to work alongside in the future.

pageCache.pageTitle: Admissions - St. John's C of E Primary School
pageCache.text:
Admissions
Home | For Parents | Admissions
Admission arrangements are made by Kent County Council (KCC) and parents apply for a place for their child in school via the Reception Common Admissions Form, on which they can name up to three chosen schools. A place is then offered direct from KCC.
You can view our current and next academic year policies under our Policies area of the website.
Children are admitted to school during the academic year in which they are five years old.
At St John’s, we have an agreed intake of 60 children into our EYFS (Reception) classes, who are mainly welcomed into the school at the start of the Autumn term, although a deferred start can be discussed.
Governors have agreed the headteacher may increase class sizes to a maximum of 32 (64 for each year group) in KS2 (years 3-6).
When Should My Child Start School?
https://www.kent.gov.uk/education-and-children/schools/school-age
Children Starting School September 2027
Do you have a child born between 1st Sept 2022 and 31st August 2023?If so, please apply for a place online at: www.kent.gov.uk/ola before Friday 15th January 2027.
Application for Primary Intake opens Friday 6th November 2026 and closes Friday 15th January 2027.
Apply at : http://www.kent.gov.uk/ola
Whilst the closing date for KCC (Kent County Council) to receive applications is Friday 15th January 2027 applications that are submitted no later than Thursday 11th February 2027 for a good reason will be treated as “on time” if it is reasonably practicable to accept them. These applications must be received no later than Thursday 11th February 2027. Please speak to Primary Admissions for more advice on 03000 412121.
Applications received after Thursday 11th February 2027 but before Friday 30th April 2027 will not receive a school offer on Friday 16th April 2027. KCC will consider these reallocation applications with applicants that have joined a school’s waiting list on the reallocation date of Thursday 27th May 2027. If none of the schools you have expressed a preference for on a reallocation application can be offered to you, KCC will offer you an alternative school. They will also advise you on your right to appeal against this decision and place you on the waiting list of any schools you named that were a higher preference than the school you were offered.
After Thursday 27th May 2027 you can request to go on any school’s waiting list and if places become available, we will offer directly to parents. KCC will not make any further offersApplications made after Thursday 27th May 2027 should be made directly to the school.
School Tours for Reception Age Children
School tours for parents of Reception age children open September 2026 and run until the end of November 2026.
To request a visit please either email; office@st-johns-maidstone.kent sch.uk or call us on 01622 735916.
Oversubscription criteria
If the number of preferences for St John’s is more than the 60 spaces available, places will be allocated in the following priority order:
If you are interested in applying for a place at St John’s for your child, please contact the school and we will arrange for you to visit in the Autumn Term. Please contact Mrs Holt on 01622 735916 who will make an appointment for you to be taken on a tour of the school and visit classrooms where children are working.
Health and special access reasons
In Year Admission Applications
If you wish to apply for a school place at St John’s Church of England Primary School or transfer between schools during the school year, please see full details of our admissions arrangements below before completing an In Year Admission Form.
If you child has an EHCP (Educational and Health Care Plan) please contact your named SEN Officer or SEND area team. Email: Senwest@kent.gov.uk Tel: 03000 420 997
The completed form can be brought into the school office, posted to us or emailed: office@st-johns-maidstone.kent.sch.uk
We aim to notify parents of the outcome of their application in writing within 10 school days, during term time
Appeals
(For information in regard to Admission Appeals For Year R September 2027, please see below)
We are bound to inform you that it is your right to appeal against the governors’ decision not to offer a place to your child. If you wish to appeal please write to:
Clerk to the GovernorsSt John’s CEP SchoolProvender WayWeaveringMaidstoneKent ME14 5TZ
In accordance to the Admission Appeals Code 2022 Admission (paragraphs 2.1 to 2.4) authorities must set a timetable for organising and hearing appeal that:
a) includes a deadline for lodging appeals which allows appellants at least 20 schooldays from the date of notification that their application was unsuccessful toprepare and lodge their written appeal;
b) ensures that appellants receive at least 10 school days’ notice of their appealhearing;
c) includes reasonable deadlines for appellants to submit additional evidence, foradmission authorities to submit their evidence, and for the clerk to send appealpapers to the panel and parties;
d) ensures that decision letters are sent within five school days of the hearingwherever possible.
Here are the deadlines for hearing different types of appeals:
Deadline for hearing appeal
Applications made in the normal admissions round
Within 40 school days of the deadline for lodging appeals
Within 40 school days of the deadline for lodging appeals, or within 30 school days of the appeal being lodged
Applications for in-year admissions
Within 30 school days of the appeal being lodged
Any appeals submitted after the appropriate deadline must still be heard, in accordance with whatever timescale is set out in the timetable published by the admission authority.
Admission Appeal For Year R September 2027
If your child is due to start Primary school in September 2027, you can appeal if you are refused a place at one of your preferred schools on National Offer Day (Friday, 16th April 2027).
You needed to submit your appeal before Monday, 17th May 2027 for it to be considered by Monday 19th July 2027. Any appeals received after this time will be heard within 40 school days from the deadline, or where reasonably possible in line with updated guidance from the Department for Education.
For late applications, appeals should be heard within 40 school days from the deadline for lodging appeals where possible, or within 30 school days of the appeal being lodged where reasonably possible in line with updated guidance from the Department for Education.
St John's C of E Primary School

Music
Home | Learning | Music
We play musical instruments, make them, find out how they work, learn songs and use both sheet music and digital music to learn.
It’s an important part of life and allows creativity for our children, to experiment with sound and notes to play something truly unique.
Young Voices
Each year, we take the children from the choir to perform in Young Voices, the world's largest choir, at the O2 Arena. It’s an incredibly inspiring experience for them, and it's amazing to see them creating lifelong memories as they sing and dance with all their heart!
What our parents had to say:
"The children were absolutely fantastic and so well behaved. It was so lovely to see them living their best lives!"

pageCache.pageTitle: Young Carers - St. John's C of E Primary School
pageCache.text:
Young Carers
At St John’s, we take pride in the recognition, care and support we offer for our Young Carers.
Who are Young Carers?
‘Young carers are children who look after a friend or family member. Their extra responsibilities often mean they miss out on school and hanging out with friends. It can sideline their whole childhood. These children often need space to enjoy being young and need support into adulthood so they can pursue their dreams outside of caring.’
(The Children’s Society)
There are over 800 000 young carers in England and 1 in 10 are aged under 10. At St John’s , we have children from Y1 to Y6 fulfilling this role and we know there are many more who don’t realise they are!
Being a young carer can have a big impact on a young person’s life.
What might a young carer do?
· Practical tasks, such as cooking, housework or shopping.
· Physical care, such as helping someone out of bed.
· Emotional support, such as talking to someone who is distressed.
· Personal care, such as helping someone dress.
· Managing the family budget and collecting prescriptions.
· Helping to five medicine.
· Helping someone communicate.
· Looking after brothers and sisters.
If you would like to speak to anyone, or receive more information, please contact Mrs Gee via the school office.
St John's C of E Primary School

pageCache.pageTitle: Collective Worship - St. John's C of E Primary School
pageCache.text:
Collective Worship
Christian Distinctiveness
Sing to the Lord, all the world! Worship the Lord with joy; come before him with happy songs!
Collective Worship at St John's
Our daily act of Christian Collective Worship strengthens and supports the Christian identity of our school, reaffirms our vision and associated values of Friendship, Forgiveness, Trust and Compassion and celebrates the central role that each person has to play in our community. Our worship reflects the variety of traditions found in the Church of England and will recognise and follow the Christian liturgical year.
What does Worship look like at St John's?
Worship is led by a number of staff, children and visitors and is an important part of the school day. Using a variety of sung worship, prayer, drama, storytelling, videos, liturgy and art the community is encouraged to reflect on the teachings of the Bible and on big questions about what it means to be human and the role God might play in that.
Worship at St John's is inclusive and open to all, those with Christian faith, other faith or none. Together we come as a community to enjoy a time of peace, wonderment and contemplation. It is interactive, all who are present are encouraged to take part where they feel able and contribute their own thoughts and ideas when possible. The photos below show just some examples of our Worship and reflection times at St John's.
St John's C of E Primary School

pageCache.pageTitle: Interactive Prayer Tree - St. John's C of E Primary School
pageCache.text:
Interactive Prayer Tree
Christian Distinctiveness
Be anxious for nothing, but in everything by prayer and supplication, with thanksgiving, let your requests be made known to God; and the peace of God, which surpasses all understanding, will guard your hearts and minds through Christ Jesus.
Our central prayer space at St John's
Our prayer tree is an interactive mural for the use of all stakeholders.
Prayers are grouped into three main types;Red Leaf – prayers for ourselves, friends, family and colleagues.Gold Leaf- prayers for those around the world who are unknown to us.Green Leaf- prayers for the wonders of God’s creation.
The mural itself features our four core Christion values which help us ’live out’ our vision. Within the roots of the tree, Christian symbols are featured to stimulate discussion, thought and to remind us that as a school we are ‘rooted’ in Christian theology and the teachings of Jesus.The last line of our vision arcs across the tree mural, reminding us that through developing our spirituality through reflection and prayer we can ‘Grow beyond all we can imagine’.
Using the Prayer Tree
The Prayer Tree at St John's is constantly changing as new prayers are written by the school community. Below are just some examples of the tree being used by our pupils and a selection of prayers written.

pageCache.pageTitle: Our Core Christians Values - St. John's C of E Primary School
pageCache.text:
Our Core Christians Values
Christian Distinctiveness
Friendship
Since they could not get him to Jesus because of the crowd, they made an opening in the roof above Jesus by digging through it and then lowered the mat the man was lying on. When Jesus saw their faith, he said to the paralysed man, “Son, your sins are forgiven.”
Forgiveness
“My son,’ the father said, ‘you are always with me, and everything I have is yours. But we had to celebrate and be glad, because this brother of yours was dead and is alive again; he was lost and is found.”
Trust
He got up, rebuked the wind and said to the waves, “Quiet! Be still!”Then the wind died down and it was completely calm. He said to his disciples, “Why are you so afraid? Do you still have no faith?”
Compassion
“Which of these three do you think was a neighbour to the man who fell into the hands of robbers?” The expert in the law replied, “The one who had mercy on him.” Jesus told him, “Go and do likewise.”
At St John’s we believe that it is not enough to talk about the core values and know what the Bible says about them. The Christian faith tells us that human beings are created in the image of God, and that we should all use our power, skills and resources for the good of all, thus we need to put our beliefs into action. We strive to ensure that our values are lived out in the day to day life of the school community and beyond.
Value Champions
We acknowledge pupils who demonstrate our values day by day in school. Each term every class is asked to nominate a pupil who they feel lives out the Christian values. The class teacher writes a paragraph about why the child has been nominated and it is displayed in the hall along with a photograph. The names of these children are then printed in the school newsletter.
St John's C of E Primary School

pageCache.pageTitle: Religious Education - St. John's C of E Primary School
pageCache.text:
Religious Education
Christian Distinctiveness
Jesus replied: “‘Love the Lord your God with all your heart and with all your soul and with all your mind.’ This is the first and greatest commandment. And the second is like it: ‘Love your neighbour as yourself.’
At St John’s C of E Primary School we aspire to ensure that every child whose journey in life takes them through our school leaves as a successful learner, conscientious steward of the earth and respectful individual. We aim for our pupils to be able to move forward in an ever developing society to make a positive contribution, wherever their path may take them.
Religious Education seeks to make a major contribution to the spiritual, moral, social and cultural development of pupils by helping them to acquire the knowledge and understanding of Christianity and the other major religions represented in Britain. It also helps them to develop their own beliefs and values.
R.E plays a very important part in our broad, balanced and coherent curriculum to which all pupils are entitled at St John’s. Through using a variety of teaching techniques such as drama, art, discussion, use of artefacts, stories, pictures, periods of stillness and reflection, pupils have opportunities to learn both about religion and from religion. RE is taught following the Kent Agreed Syllabus.
We are very proud of the RE learning that happens throughout our school. Here are just some examples of the amazing RE working walls, displays, artwork and written pieces that the children have created within their RE lessons.
St John's C of E Primary School

pageCache.pageTitle: House Captains - St. John's C of E Primary School
pageCache.text:
House Captains
Home | For Children | House Captains
Meet our house captains who are all Year 6 pupils.
We have a boy and a girl representative for each of our houses.
Aquila
Pegasus
Phoenix
Ursa
They are working hard to be good role models to all our children and have been elected to the role by their peers as someone they respect, trust and feel they can talk to.
House Points
House points are collected throughout the academic year and will be added to those gained on Sports Day. This means that Sports Day will no longer just be about the actual physical side of PE and physical activity but also the effort and values that we can show both within our PE lessons, clubs and our classrooms.
Showing our Christian Core Values (CCV) and PE values is as important as scoring the goals and winning the races. We may not all be the best runners, throwers or jumpers but we can all show the best attitudes to working in a team, winning and losing and showing resilience and this will now all contribute to securing the House cups this year!
How pupils gain house points:
- Showing the PE values: determination, honesty, respect, passion, team-work, self-belief
- Showing our CCV: Friendship, forgiveness, trust, compassion
- Completing their weekly reading challenge 'Give Me 5'
- Following the school rules: Be ready, be safe, be respectful
Each week the House captains will collect the house points from each class and these will be added to a running total that Miss Clapperton, our P.E. Lead, will share with staff and parents via the school newsletter.
St John's C of E Primary School

pageCache.pageTitle: Well-being - St. John's C of E Primary School
pageCache.text:
Well-being
Home | For Children | Well-being
Our children are all well cared for, nurtured and cherished through mutually respectful relationships built on the firm foundation of our four core Christian values of Friendship, Forgiveness, Trust and Compassion.We think these are fantastic life skills to take forward in every aspect of their lives.
As a result, strong bonds of trust and very positive attachments are made between pupils and staff, creating a safe space for our children to express themselves, ask questions and think deeply.
The wellbeing of our children and staff is our number one priority and we have processes in place to ensure everyone is listened to, where open and honest discussion can easily take place.
The Sanctuary is an area for times of quiet reflection, stillness and prayer which has been built in harmony with nature within the school grounds.
Our children are encouraged just to ‘be’ in tranquil contemplation and replenish their wellbeing.
Our Interactive Prayer Tree is a constantly changing mural where our children are encouraged to pray for themselves, friends, family colleagues, those unknown to them around the world and for the wonders of God’s creation. The tree reminds them that by developing their spirituality through reflection and prayer, they can ‘grow beyond all we can imagine’.
St John's C of E Primary School
